deliverables.presentation_rule: Examples publish unrounded semantic expected values and separately publish any display value/precision. A rounded display is never the calculation oracle.

promotion_rules: Record immutable source/revision, route, units, scope/applicability, canonical inputs, expected unrounded outputs or stated source precision, code-data revision and an independent reconstruction.
Resolve amendment or dataset disagreement through the PF2 F10 migration ledger before promotion.
A qualified reviewer validates reconstruction and provenance before SB-PROMOTED-E4; E6 approval remains a separate scoped record.
Corrected, disputed, partial, unsupported and narrative-only records cannot be numerical oracle assertions, though they may remain diagnostic/taxonomy fixtures.
Promotion applies only to the declared operation/profile/case; one example cannot stand in for missing nodes, interiors, boundaries or invalid/unsupported paths.
Every fixture binds semantic operation, schema, profile, code-data, expected state/value, tolerance and evidence identifiers.
deliverables.source_data_verification: Normalize each approved table/figure only within an operation scope; dual-review source transcription, units, nodes, interpolation/cap rules and digest; replay all node/interior/boundary fixtures before the data revision can be used.

classes.rule: first compare the unrounded reconstructed value under T1/T2, then separately require agreement within half the least-significant source increment unless source uncertainty states otherwise
apply the exact code/construction comparison to raw values and test exact/inside/outside; tolerance may diagnose runtime drift but cannot turn fail into pass
use decimal arithmetic, explicit rate precision and named currency rounding stage; engineering floating tolerance cannot alter totals

deliverables.method_specific_rule: A numerical method may declare a tighter or different absolute floor only with an oracle-error analysis and stable tolerance ID; it cannot loosen a code or construction decision boundary.
deliverables.parity_rule: Report both independently expected error and Python/.NET difference. A small cross-language difference does not pass a case when both implementations miss the oracle.

rules.rule: Freeze expected_leaf_set from effective inputs, required-check profile, topology, code-data revision and applicability conditions before evaluation; each entry has stable required_check_id, requirement status, applicability predicate and identity.
Retain one leaf result for every expected entry in member result, candidate, export and report. Omitted, failed or not-applicable leaves cannot disappear.
Qualified requires every required leaf to be completed, applicable, pass, complete_for_scope and current, all bound to one effective member revision.
A required not_evaluated leaf makes the result partial/unqualified and emits CHECK.REQUIRED_NOT_EVALUATED.
A required not_applicable leaf remains visible and makes the result partial/unqualified. If genuinely outside scope, the profile/topology must exclude it before expected_leaf_set is frozen.

A profile-excluded non-required leaf may be not_applicable only with a proven recorded predicate. Unknown applicability, stale/unbound, rejection, cancellation or software error never satisfies exclusion.
Any required fail makes the member engineering fail. Any required invalid, incomplete, stale or unbound result makes it partial/unqualified. Approval cannot override calculation state.

Optimization ranks only candidates satisfying AGG-03 and publishes all domain members with reason-coded exclusions, expected leaf set and completeness. Partial enumeration cannot claim optimum or total infeasibility.
Selected and scheduled reinforcement are rechecked as separate supplied arrangements; required-area checks alone cannot qualify fabrication or construction outputs.
The aggregate returns governing failures/locations and all non-success diagnostics without replacing leaf provenance or identities.

deliverables.current_foundation_disposition: Current CandidateRanker correctly excludes required NotEvaluated and NotApplicable outcomes, but collapses missing and those two states into one unevaluated ID list and trusts an externally supplied required-check list. Before promotion beyond E2 it must consume the frozen expected_leaf_set and preserve reason/state evidence.
acceptance_cases: required pass plus optional not_applicable qualifies only when the optional exclusion predicate is proven
required not_applicable is partial and unqualified
required missing/not_evaluated is partial and unqualified
additional explicit fail is infeasible even when omitted from required IDs
partial search returns best-so-far wording only and no optimum claim
